clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad: which code path the traces and the committed state come from, read in the v0.16.7 source that the endpoints report (Monad/0.16.7).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched the three files from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/ and read the cited lines. category/rpc/monad_executor.cpp:1306-1309 declares vm::VM vm_{vm::VM::InterpreterOnly} with a comment that the compiler can misreport out-of-gas errors, and 1824 builds BlockState block_state{tdb, vm_} on the parent block state. cmd/monad/main.cpp:485-488 builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual}. category/execution/runloop/runloop_monad.cpp:125-155 hashes each delayed execution result header with keccak256 of its RLP and compares it with the locally computed block hash, and 680-681 wraps it in MONAD_ASSERT. So the 20,000 traced transactions ran on the interpreter, and validators without trace_calls run the Dual (compiled) path. The tie between the two is the committed state comparison plus the consensus assertion, as the item says. The item correctly leaves open whether rpc.monad.xyz runs with trace_calls; if it does, the committed state comparison is interpreter against interpreter and only the assertion ties it to compiled validators. That gap is recorded as a lead in the research file, so the clearing is worded no wider than its evidence.

clearedSpotChecks.check: HyperEVM producer check. The traces come from the public replica https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31); the official endpoint answers eth_getStorageAt with the latest value whatever block is named, so the last traced post value of every PoolManager word was compared with the official latest state.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran eth_getStorageAt for PoolManager 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F, slot 0x42391778c932d66173daeeb1a6bb2980f717afa36392c04ced59f639200a247e. On https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm it returned 0 at blocks 0x316b0ff, 0x316b100 and latest. On https://rpc.purroofgroup.com it returned 0 at 0x316b0ff, 0x1239bc2b12e04 at 0x316b100 and 0 at latest. The official endpoint therefore ignores the block tag, as the item says, and a per-block comparison against it is void. eth_getBalance of the PoolManager on the official endpoint at latest (head 0x31dc794, block 52283284, later than the official head 52271283 the unit recorded) returned 0x9d908ef23bc0864f, which is 11353731831636723279 wei and equals the recorded traced final balance. eth_getStorageAt slot 0 returns owner 0x2d09d0c2f82c59b19b3c65a48ce2c550bf0921f9, consistent with the constructor write in src/PoolManager.sol:101. The check covers only the last value of each word, which the item states and the research file carries as a medium lead.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Reading of unlock when the callback returns data whose first word is 0.
clearedSpotChecks.note: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 assigns result = IUnlockCallback(msg.sender).unlockCallback(data) with result typed bytes memory. The ABI decoder reads the head word as the offset of the bytes value; an offset of 0 points at the head word itself, whose value 0 is read as the length, so result is empty bytes and no revert happens. The NonzeroDeltaCount check at line 112 runs after the decode in every case, so the reading of the return data cannot skip settlement. This agrees with the item and with the chain behaviour it reports. I also read the non-native settle branch at src/PoolManager.sol:355-361 (msg.value must be 0, paid is the balance rise since sync), which is the A2 assumption the Polygon rebasing note relies on.
